six_targets.limitation: Chronic ethanol-associated pantothenate depletion and rescue affected acetylcholine synthesis in rats; this does not establish that extra B5 raises brain acetylcholine in adequately nourished humans.

six_targets.biological_role: Folate-dependent methyl metabolism helps maintain the brain choline resource available for acetylcholine formation; folate deprivation lowered choline and acetylcholine in studied mouse models, with SAM rescue supporting this upstream resource relationship.
six_targets.dietary_input_note: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added.
six_targets.limitation: Animal evidence is conditional on age, brain region and experimental context. Choline and acetylcholine concentrations were measured; methyl-dependent choline retention and the consequence for synthesis capacity are mechanistic inferences, not measured human synthesis flux. Folate is not a ChAT cofactor; extra folate above adequacy and cognitive benefit are not established.

relationship.pm_biological_role: Inadequate one-carbon donor availability can increase pressure on choline-dependent methyl donation and disturb brain choline and acetylcholine availability, thereby constraining the substrate capacity used for acetylcholine synthesis.
relationship.evidence_limitation: The mapping is supported by dietary and genetic animal models plus the established choline substrate reaction. It does not show that folate, B12, or betaine supplementation increases acetylcholine synthesis in nutrient-replete humans, and it does not inherit the KC food list.

constituent_relationships.label: Vitamin B9 (folate)
constituent_relationships.reader_description: Folate-dependent methyl metabolism helps maintain the choline available for acetylcholine formation in the studied deficiency models.

adjudications.applicability_proposition: Inadequacy of the shared methyl-donor pool can constrain this mechanism’s governed acetylcholine-synthesis capacity.
established_links: Choline plus acetyl-CoA forms acetylcholine via choline acetyltransferase (PM6-F2).
Dietary folate deficiency reduced brain choline and acetylcholine in mouse models, and SAM restored both under folate compromise (PM6-F6).
Methionine-synthase-reductase deficiency lowered hippocampal choline, betaine, and acetylcholine (PM6-F6).
A separate folate-deficiency experiment found region- and age-dependent acetylcholine changes rather than a uniform whole-brain response (PM6-F6).
adjudications.rationale: Type D is met through a supported mechanistic chain rather than a single end-to-end human capacity assay: one-carbon compromise changes the choline resource state, animal models show lower choline and acetylcholine under folate or methionine-cycle impairment, and choline is the required synthesis substrate. BRS1(KC1) was screened out because choline is not a LAT1 large-neutral-amino-acid cargo.

kc_atom.biological_role: Provides 5-methyltetrahydrofolate, the methyl-group donor used by methionine synthase to remethylate homocysteine and replenish methionine for SAM synthesis.
kc_atom.evidence_limitation: Folate insufficiency can constrain remethylation and methylation capacity, but effects on SAM, SAH and downstream methylation vary by tissue and metabolic state; adequacy does not imply benefit from additional intake.
